title: Autopatch quality update policies: per-type approvals override ring deferrals
summary: In Windows Autopatch, one Intune quality update policy can now manage Windows quality updates, .NET Framework updates and quick machine recovery (QMR) updates. Each type gets automatic approval (with a 0–30 day deferral) or manual approval. New reports show quality update status and QMR boot-failure remediation. QMR updates default to manual approval.
why: The policy's deferral replaces the deferral in your update ring or Autopatch group instead of adding to it. A 5-day ring plus a 2-day policy means 2 days, not 7. With manual approval there is no deferral, and devices install as soon as you approve. Deadlines and grace periods still come from the ring.
todo: Before you create a quality update policy, write down the effective deferral per ring. To keep your current timing, create one policy per ring with the same deferral and assignment.
Decide who approves optional and out-of-band updates (for example this month's slmgr OOB fix) and how quickly.
If you created a hotpatch quality update policy before approvals existed, open it, review the approval settings and save it.
